Subject: High error rate - eu-west dedicated pool

Hi Jasmine,

We're seeing sustained 502/503 spikes from our eu-west Dedicated pool starting ~09:45 UTC. Token throughput dropped and several requests timed out — roughly 18% error rate for the last 20 minutes. Attached a small sample of request traces and the allocator snapshot (euw-sample-traces.txt).

Can you confirm whether there's any throttling or autoscaler activity on your side? This is impacting our staging and a small percentage of production traffic. We're happy to provide more traces if it helps.

I'm temporarily routing new requests away from the affected reservation and enabling a warm-standby pool to reduce visible errors.

Can you confirm: did the failing requests share similar sequence lengths or spikes in concurrency? That will help us prioritize KV-cache and batching checks.

I've looped in Ben (ops lead) and Diego (serving runtime) to help with logs and a postmortem. We'll follow up with a summary and an ETA for a permanent fix within 48 hours.

Subject: Internal: eu-west autoscaler starvation - quick root cause and action items

Team,

Summary (internal): we traced the outage to an autoscaler race that led to under-provisioning for a tenant-heavy reservation. Sequence of events:
- 09:41 UTC: a short concurrency spike from DataPulse triggered eviction logic while the allocator was still reconciling instance claims.
- 09:42-09:55 UTC: autoscaler attempted to scale up but several warm nodes failed to attach due to a transient AMI pull latency; our fallback code considered those nodes 'unavailable' and started additional evictions, compounding starvation.
- 09:47 UTC: KV cache warmup didn't complete for a subset of shards, causing high token-generation latency and timeouts reported as 502s.

Impact: ~18% errors for DataPulse across eu-west dedicated reservation for ~25 minutes. No data exfiltration.

Immediate mitigations we already applied:
- Rerouted new DataPulse requests to our eu-north warm standby from 10:00 UTC; error rate dropped to baseline by 10:06 UTC.
- Disabled aggressive eviction heuristics and bumped minimal headroom for the affected reservation.

Planned fixes (timeline):
1) Patch autoscaler to avoid dual-actions when warm-node attach is pending — roll to prod by 2027-03-08 (Diego).
2) Add AMI pull latency detection with fallback to alternative images/regions — prioritized Q2.
3) Improve KV-cache telemetry and make warmup atomic per-shard (observable by tenant) — Q2.
4) Run a chaos-style test to reproduce warm-node attach delays and validate fallback paths — scheduled 2027-03-15 (Ops).

Customer comms: Jasmine, propose the following: postmortem summary, 25% service credit for the impacted billing week, and an invitation to a technical debrief with Diego next week.

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident summary — eu-west dedicated pool disruption (Mar 2)

Hi Omar / Erin,

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated the eu-west disruption on Mar 2. Below is a concise post-incident summary and next steps.

What happened
- Between 09:41–10:06 UTC on 2027-03-02, your eu-west reservation experienced increased error rates (~18%) driven by a combination of eviction activity and delayed warm-node attachments during an autoscaler reaction to a short concurrency spike.

Root cause (short):
- A timing race in the autoscaler combined with transient image-pull latency caused nodes that were still attaching to be treated as unavailable, which triggered additional evictions and prevented sufficient warm capacity from coming online. This, in turn, delayed KV-cache warmup for some request paths and caused token-generation timeouts.

What we did
- Immediate: routed traffic to eu-north warm-standby and disabled aggressive eviction heuristics for your reservation (09:58–10:06 UTC).
- Investigation: collected allocator state, scheduler traces, and KV-cache warmup logs (attached).
- Remediation: patched the autoscaler to hold off on eviction decisions while node-attach is pending; deployed a targeted hotfix to eu-west on 2027-03-08.

What you'll see next
- A hotfix deployed 2027-03-08 to prevent the autoscaler race.
- Additional telemetry and a follow-on change to make warm-node attach failures degrade gracefully (Q2).
- A scheduled technical debrief with our serving runtime engineer (Diego) on 2027-03-11 at 14:00 UTC — please confirm availability.

Compensation
- We're offering a 25% credit for the impacted billing week. We'll apply this automatically and send a billing note to your finance contact.

Attachments included: euw-autoscale-logs.tar.gz (aggregated traces), postmortem-draft-20270308.md (detailed internal postmortem).

If you'd like a live walkthrough of the logs and the fixes, Diego is happy to join the debrief. Again — apologies for the disruption. We're taking this seriously and will share progress as the follow-on Q2 work is scheduled.

Best,
